name: plist_read
description: Read XML and binary property lists (plistlib) and return them as JSON: dates converted from the Apple epoch to ISO 8601 UTC, UID references kept as {_uid}, a binary value as its length and kind only. A structural reading, not an interpretation: an NSKeyedArchiver object graph is not resolved, a .btm file is shown as the structure it has, not as a list of login items, and a date is plistlib's conversion (microsecond resolution, the raw float not kept). SENSITIVE: a plist can hold a password verifier (an account plist: ShadowHashData, Kerberos keys, a hint), a token or a password. No binary value is printed, hashed or previewed (no digest, no base64, no head), and a value under a key whose name marks it secret-bearing (verifier, Kerberos keys, password, passphrase, secret, token, credential, private key, hint) is withheld at any depth and when `key` selects it: the answer carries a locator (finding_id, key path, kind, length). A value under any other key is printed as it is, so read an account plist as a job with secret_output: true, or select the keys the question needs. write_values: true (refused outside a job) creates $OUT/plist-values.jsonl, mode 0600, before it reads anything (a file or link already there is refused) and writes the withheld and binary values there and nowhere else, a binary value as base64 up to max_blob bytes with its whole length beside it. Reads one file, or every .plist and .btm file under a directory in sorted order (links are not followed). One file at a time: each file's row is written as it is read, a file that does not parse, is over max_file_bytes or max_nodes, or nests deeper than max_depth is that file's failed or skipped row with the reason, and files not reached before max_seconds are counted and named, so status is complete only when every matched file was read. `extracted_file_mtime` is the mtime of the file as read, a working copy's, not the original's. A rerun of the same sweep that finds fewer files does not replace a larger earlier page file: it writes a new name and says which earlier file it kept.

path.description: A .plist or .btm file, or a directory to walk (links inside it are not followed)

key.description: Return only this top-level key, or a dotted path into the structure (array items by index). A path through a secret-bearing key name is withheld too

max_blob.description: Bytes of a binary value written to the values file, base64 (default 4096). It never affects the answer: no binary value is printed

limit.description: Files shown inline (default 200, and at most max_inline_bytes of them). All are counted; the whole result is in out_file, or, when that is omitted, in a file under work/<your id>/tool-output/ (in a job, $OUT/tool-output/) that the answer names

out_file.description: JSONL path for every file's row, one per line as each file is read. The tool does not overwrite: an existing file or link at that name is refused

write_values.description: Write each binary and withheld value to $OUT/plist-values.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; the file is created first and an existing file or link is refused; the answer never carries a value

max_file_bytes.description: A file larger than this is skipped, named, and not read (default 33554432)

max_nodes.description: A file (or the part `key` selects) with more values than this is skipped, named, and not converted (default 200000)

max_depth.description: A tree nested deeper than this is skipped, named, and not converted (default 100)

max_seconds.description: Stop starting new files after this many seconds (default 90); the files not reached are counted and the first are named

max_inline_bytes.description: The inline answer is cut at this many bytes of rows as well as at `limit` rows (default 1048576): the page is the rows before the first that does not fit, the whole is in out_file or the file the answer names
